name: Fixed-size sliding window on a circular array
whenToUse: The standard answer: one pass, one running sum, indices wrap with % n.

card.signals: "the sum of the next k numbers" (or previous -k) for every i: each sum is a window of |k| numbers in a row, and the windows of i and i + 1 share |k| − 1 numbers. "code is circular": the window wraps from the end back to the start.
card.pattern: a fixed-size window that moves around a circle. Build the window of code[0] once, then move it one step for each next i: one number enters on the right, one leaves on the left. Indices wrap with % n, so after n − 1 comes 0.
card.coreIdea: keep total, the sum of the window. Moving the window costs one addition and one subtraction, not |k| additions. All numbers change at the same time, so write the sums into a new result array and do not change code.

invariant: Before result[i] is written, the window code[left..right] (with wrap) holds exactly the |k| numbers next to code[i], and total is their sum.
